title: 3sum
description:
Given an integer array nums, return all the triplets [nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]] such that i != j, i != k, and j != k, and nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0.
Notice that the solution set must not contain duplicate triplets.Print each triplet enclosed in brackets, separated by a space. You must sort the elements inside each triplet in ascending order. Furthermore, you must print the triplets sorted in lexicographical (ascending) order

examples.explanation:
nums[0] + nums[1] + nums[2] = (-1) + 0 + 1 = 0.
nums[1] + nums[2] + nums[4] = 0 + 1 + (-1) = 0.
nums[0] + nums[3] + nums[4] = (-1) + 2 + (-1) = 0.
The distinct triplets are [-1,0,1] and [-1,-1,2].
Notice that the order of the output and the order of the triplets does not matter.
The only possible triplet does not sum up to 0.
The only possible triplet sums up to 0.
